name: directory.delete
description: Delete a directory. Empty directories require no flags. Pass `recursive: true` to delete a directory and all its contents (analogous to `rm -rf`). Hard delete — bypasses Recycle Bin / Trash.

recursive.description: If true, recursively delete the directory's contents before removing the directory itself. Without this flag, removing a non-empty directory returns ERR not_empty.

entries_removed.description: Count of files + subdirectories removed inside the target when `recursive: true`. 0 for a non-recursive empty-directory removal.

x-implementations.name: remove_directory_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RemoveDirectoryW` for the empty-directory case. With `recursive: true`, the agent performs a depth-first walk via FindFirstFileW / FindNextFileW + DeleteFileW for files + RemoveDirectoryW for subdirectories. Reparse points are NOT traversed — `recursive` removes the link, not the link target.

x-implementations.name: remove_directory_a
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RemoveDirectoryA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x. Same recursive walk pattern with the ANSI variants.

windows-modern.description: RemoveDirectoryW for the empty case. Recursive walk uses FindFirstFileW / FindNextFileW + DeleteFileW for files + RemoveDirectoryW for subdirectories. Reparse points (symlinks, junctions, mount points) are removed without traversal — protects against accidentally deleting the link target.

windows-classic.description: RemoveDirectoryW on NT 5+; RemoveDirectoryA on NT 4 / 9x. Same recursive walk pattern. Pre-NT-5 has no reparse points, so the no-traversal protection is moot.
